prompt: What rank did Hermann Goring hold in the Luftwaffe during World War II, before Robert Ritter von Greim, and how does this rank compare to the equivalent ranks in other branches of the German military?
answer:
During World War II, Hermann Göring held the rank of **Reichsmarschall des Großdeutschen Reiches** (“Reich Marshal of the Greater German Reich”). Adolf Hitler created this rank specifically for Göring in **July 1940**, and Göring was its only holder.

He remained commander-in-chief of the Luftwaffe until **Robert Ritter von Greim** replaced him in the final days of the war. Greim was promoted to **Generalfeldmarschall** when appointed Luftwaffe commander-in-chief in April 1945.

### Comparison with other German military ranks

| Branch | Comparable senior rank |
|---|---|
| German Army (*Heer*) | **Generalfeldmarschall** — Field Marshal |
| Luftwaffe | **Generalfeldmarschall** — Field Marshal |
| German Navy (*Kriegsmarine*) | **Großadmiral** — Grand Admiral |
| Göring’s special rank | **Reichsmarschall** — above Field Marshal |

The **Reichsmarschall** rank was not simply the Luftwaffe equivalent of a field marshal. It was a unique rank **senior to all German Army and Luftwaffe field marshals** and, in status, above the Navy’s Großadmiral. Thus, Göring outranked von Greim, even though both served as Luftwaffe commander-in-chief at different times.
